analysis.title: GS Early Morning Research Recap: Ratings and Target Price Changes - November 4, 2026 as of 5:30 AM ET
key_insights: Rating changes in the Americas: Ibotta (IBTA) upgraded to Neutral from Sell after a Q3 review citing continued growth recovery, and Skyworks (SWKS) reinstated at Sell because smartphone headwinds are expected to offset the benefits of diversification and scale.

Rating changes outside the US: Gecina (GFCP.PA) downgraded to Neutral from Buy on slower pipeline lettings, Chengdu XGimi (688696.SS) upgraded to Neutral from Sell on rising overseas contribution, and Varmora Granito (VARO.BO) initiated at Neutral.
AMD (Buy) is the top Americas call of the day. GS sees datacenter strength translating to 80% growth in 2027 despite PC headwinds.
Block (XYZ, Buy, on the Conviction List) posted a solid 3Q26 beat and raise. GS says preliminary 2027 guidance is likely to support the stock.

Several AI hardware names printed beat-and-raise quarters with positive 2027 outlooks: Arista (ANET) with a strong initial 2027 outlook, Super Micro (SMCI) on broadening demand with improving working capital, and AMD.

Payments and fintech 3Q26 takeaways were mostly constructive. Block, Flywire (positive guidance revision on a top and bottom line beat) and Marqeta (beat on lower opex with in-line top line) were positive. Toast had a solid quarter with few surprises, Fiserv reiterated its outlook with improved retention trends, and Upstart cut its volume outlook on macro headwinds.

Target price cuts of 10% or more in the US: Aptiv (APTV) to $54 from $61, People Inc. (PPLI) to $56 from $63, Ultragenyx (RARE) to $17 from $19, Ramaco (METC) to $7 from $8 and Upstart (UPST) to $24 from $28. Increases: Gartner (IT) to $207 from $181, Amgen (AMGN) to $536 from $481 and Ibotta (IBTA) to $58 from $35.

Outside the US, Alstom (ALSO.PA) stays at Sell with the target cut to €9.00 from €15.50 after a profit warning. Coloplast (Sell) target rises to Dkr 450 from Dkr 400. Champion Iron (CIA.AX, Buy) target falls to A$2.90 from A$4.50 and Kakaopay (377300.KS, Neutral) target falls to W38,000 from W58,000.

Driven Brands (DRVN) is delaying 3Q results after additional material errors were identified, and lowered its FY26 EBITDA guidance. Once Upon a Farm (OFRM) estimates were lowered for the Tractor Wheels recall.
Healthcare earnings were strong. Teva posted another beat and raise, Madrigal (MDGL) reached first GAAP profitability on Rezdiffra momentum, and Tarsus reported another Xdemvy beat and raise.

Consumer and TMT reviews: Booking (BKNG) had a solid result with long-framing around the AI opportunity set, Duolingo (DUOL) showed strong bookings momentum after a user turnaround, and Phoenix Education (PXED) cited persistent AI search pressure with a weaker F2027 outlook.

Energy: Asia refining margins for 2027 are viewed as robust even in near-term de-escalation scenarios, with Buy on S-Oil (Conviction List) and Thai Oil. Saudi Aramco (Buy) beat on net income with strong cash flow.
Japan autos: Thailand raising tariffs on imported BEVs from 10% to 35% is positive for Japanese automakers.

Macro and strategy items to focus on today: US Election Monitor final update, a European Daily on more inflation and weaker growth into the winter, and Strategy Matters on why Europe's earnings defy its economy.

US midterm election events dominate today's webinar calendar, with three sessions scheduled between 8 AM and 11:30 AM ET. Two Middle East escalation and US policy sessions are scheduled for November 5.

earnings_insights: Block (XYZ) 3Q26, reported 11/3 after close: solid beat and raise per GS, with preliminary 2027 guidance likely to support the stock. No EPS figures are given in the recap.
Arista (ANET) 3Q26, reported: beat and raise with a strong initial 2027 outlook. No figures given in the recap.
Super Micro (SMCI) F1Q27, reported: beat and raise on broadening demand with improving working capital. No figures given in the recap.
AMD, reported: GS says datacenter strength translates to 80% growth in 2027 despite PC headwinds. The 80% figure is GS's forward expectation, not a reported number.
AIG 3Q26, reported: EPS beat on strong core and alternative NII, with commercial growth and margins modestly missing.
Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP), reported: healthy Q3 beat, but FY26 guidance was maintained given softer-than-expected US coffee trends.
Coca-Cola Europacific (CCEP) Q3, reported: topline beat driven by strong volumes. FY26 guidance was maintained, which GS thinks could prove conservative.
Driven Brands (DRVN): 3Q results are delayed after additional material errors were identified, and FY26 EBITDA guidance was lowered. No reported figures yet.
Upstart (UPST) 3Q26, reported: macro headwinds led to a reduced volume outlook.
Teva Q3, reported: another strong beat and raise.
Madrigal (MDGL), reported: Rezdiffra momentum drove first GAAP profitability.
Ero Copper (ERO) 3Q26, reported: beat but with some guidance downgrade.
Vonovia 9M26, reported: results were largely pre-released, with OFCF about 11% below GSe.
Alstom: GS reflects on the profit warning and stays at Sell. Iveco 3Q26 came in below GSe.
Marqeta (MQ) 3Q26, reported: beat on lower opex with relatively in-line top line trends. Flywire (FLYW) posted a top and bottom line beat with a positive guidance revision.
Phoenix Education (PXED) F4Q, reported: results highlight persistent AI search pressure, and a weaker F2027 outlook pushes recovery further out.
